source_en: Home from the library reading room.
Resident, back from the university.
Bringing my notes home. Two notebooks.
Home from my polytechnic engineering lab.
Home to my husband. He hates lateness.
Retiring from the tram depot.
The paint is peeling on your booth. Top left corner. Weeks now.
Is the air always this thick? It feels... heavy today.
Thanks. You should probably fix that light soon.
This is a mistake. I have notes. I can prove it.
Fine. In here I can keep counting without any interruption.
The pattern... there was a pattern... I almost had it...
Wait... mommy! I was so close to figuring it out...
Where are you coming from?
The library. Closed at seven. Their clock runs two minutes slow.
The medical institute. Second-year anatomy. Demanding, but I like precision.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Tired. Late hours with my notes. Stress, not a symptom. I checked.
Nothing. I sleep ten hours a night and barely notice anything.
The paint on your booth is peeling, top left. Wrong for weeks.
Your light flickers on a three-second interval. Has it always?
Anyone cross twice today?
Two. Same coat, same limp, eleven minutes apart. You stamped both.
Twice? I don't keep notes. Anatomy exams take every hour.
